title: Bought the Hereafter with the World
subtitle: A single scene changed the life of a young Qurayshi forever.
heroQuote: «Saeed ibn Aamir is a man who bought the Hereafter with the worldly life, preferring Allah and His Messenger above all else.»
intention: Read today’s journey to reflect on how a genuine moment can transform a person's life and guide them to choose the Hereafter over this world.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Saeed ibn Aamir Al-Jumahi was a young man from Quraysh, known among his people for his youth and strength. He lived in Mecca before Allah opened his heart to Islam. He did not realize that attending a particular day in Mecca would leave an indelible mark on his heart. He witnessed the execution of the Companion Khubayb ibn Adiy (may Allah be pleased with him) and saw his steadfastness and faith in the most difficult moments. That scene remained with him until it became the beginning of his path to Islam. After accepting Islam, he migrated to Medina and accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Following the Prophet's passing, he lived as an example of a just, ascetic governor who prioritized Allah's pleasure over all worldly pleasures.

steps.title: A Life-Changing Scene
steps.content:
Saeed ibn Aamir went out with the people of Mecca to witness the execution of Khubayb ibn Adiy (may Allah be pleased with him). The crowd had gathered, and the leaders of Quraysh stepped forward, each wanting to see the end of a man who remained firm in his religion. When Khubayb was brought to his execution site, he asked to be allowed to pray two units (rak'ahs) of prayer. They permitted him, so he prayed with deep humility and tranquility. He then told them that had he not feared they would think he was prolonging the prayer out of fear of death, he would have prayed longer. After that, the polytheists began bargaining with him, asking: 'Would you like Muhammad to be in your place while you are safe and free?' His answer was decisive, declaring that he would not even accept the Messenger of Allah ﷺ being pricked by a thorn while safe among his family. He then supplicated against those who gathered to kill him and surrendered his soul, steadfast and seeking Allah's reward.

This scene never left Saeed’s heart. He saw it whenever he remembered that day—seeing Khubayb steadfast while praying, hearing his words, and remembering a certainty that neither swords nor threats could shake. As days passed, he realized that such steadfastness could only be the fruit of sincere faith, and that the man loved so deeply by his companions must indeed be a Messenger from Allah.

Allah opened Saeed’s heart to Islam, so he declared his faith, indifferent to whatever hardship Quraysh might inflict upon him. He later migrated to Medina, remained close to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and witnessed goodness and whatever battles he was able to attend with him.

After the death of the Prophet ﷺ, Saeed remained upon the truth, asceticism, and honesty for which he was known. When Umar ibn Al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) assumed the Caliphate, he recognized Saeed’s standing and trustworthiness, appointing him as governor of Homs. Governance did not alter his condition; he continued to live a simple life, accumulating no wealth and seeking no worldly comforts. He spent whatever came to him on charitable causes and lived modestly with his family.

Umar visited the people of Homs and asked about their governor. They mentioned things that astonished him: that he did not come out to them early in the day, did not receive people at night, was absent for one day every month, and sometimes suffered from fainting spells. When Umar asked Saeed about this, Saeed explained that his family had no servant, so he began his day serving his household and preparing food before going out to the people. As for the night, he dedicated it purely to the worship of Allah. As for the day he was absent, it was because he washed his only garment and waited for it to dry. Regarding his fainting spells, they returned to him whenever he remembered Khubayb’s execution and his great steadfastness; he would be so overwhelmed by emotion that he would lose consciousness.

Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) rejoiced upon hearing this and praised Allah that his good opinion of Saeed was well-founded. He then sent him money to assist him, but Saeed did not view it as an opportunity to expand his living standard; rather, he considered it a trial that might distract him from his Hereafter. After consulting his wife, he distributed the money among poor Muslims and those in need, preferring what is with Allah over the pleasures of this world, just as he had done since the day his life changed while watching the steadfastness of Khubayb (may Allah be pleased with him).

steps.title: Key Lessons
steps.content:
1. Allah may make a single sincere moment the reason for a person's guidance and complete redirection of their life.
2. True faith manifests during times of hardship, as demonstrated by the steadfastness of Khubayb (may Allah be pleased with him), which deeply impacted Saeed's heart.
3. Responsibility does not mean luxury; high office can coexist with asceticism, integrity, and service to the people.
4. Whoever prioritizes the Hereafter over this world lives with a reassured heart, leaving behind a noble legacy long after they are gone.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: What is a situation where you recognized the truth, yet still delayed taking action out of fear of losing a worldly benefit or social status?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Choose a good deed you can perform today without expecting anything in return from people. Make your intention purely for Allah, bearing in mind that what is with Allah is far better and more lasting.

title: The Servant of the Prophet ﷺ
subtitle: A child presented by his mother as a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who became one of the greatest narrators of his Sunnah.
heroQuote: «O Allah, grant him wealth and children, and bless him in them.»
intention: Read today’s journey to reflect on how righteous companionship, good upbringing, and compassionate treatment can shape a person who leaves an everlasting legacy.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Anas ibn Malik Al-Ansari was a young boy when his heart filled with love for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ before ever laying eyes on him. His mother, Al-Ghumaysa' (Umm Sulaym), instilled faith in his heart and raised him to love the Prophet ﷺ, until he wished to meet him every day. Little did he know that Allah would honor him with companionship enjoyed by very few—living ten full years in the service of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, learning knowledge from him, witnessing his character, and carrying his Sunnah to generations to come.

steps.title: Ten Years in the School of Prophethood
steps.content:
Anas ibn Malik grew up in Yathrib (Medina). News of the Prophet ﷺ reached Medina before his migration, filling hearts with longing for him. The young boy listened to these reports from his mother, and his love for the Prophet ﷺ grew day after day, until he yearned to see him with his own eyes. When word spread among the people of Medina that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was on his way to them, people went out every morning waiting for his arrival. Anas would run along with the other boys toward the road, returning sad whenever he did not find him.

Then came the promised day. Medina was filled with joy, and men and children went out to welcome the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while women stood on rooftops looking for him and asking, 'Which one is he?' That day was one of the greatest days in Anas's life, and he remembered it even after passing the age of one hundred.

As soon as the Prophet ﷺ settled in Medina, Anas's mother brought her son to him and said, 'O Messenger of Allah... not a single man or woman among the Ansar remains without having given you a gift, and I find nothing to give you except this son of mine... take him, let him serve you as you wish.' The Prophet ﷺ received the boy cheerfully, wiped his head, and drew him near, marking the beginning of a journey that lasted ten full years.

Anas was ten years old, so he grew up in the household of Prophethood—observing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his worship, dealings, compassion, and manners, memorizing from his statements and actions what was not accessible to others. These years were a complete school that forged his character, filled his heart with faith, and made him one of the most knowledgeable Companions regarding the life and traits of the Prophet ﷺ.

Among the greatest memories held in Anas's mind was the noble character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said, 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had the best character among all people.' He narrated that the Prophet ﷺ once sent him on an errand, but he got distracted playing with the boys. When he looked back, he found the Prophet ﷺ standing behind him smiling, saying gently, 'O Unays (little Anas), did you go where I commanded you?' Anas heard no word of reprimand, nor saw any anger; he saw only a smile, guidance, and compassion. Years later, he said, 'By Allah, I served him for ten years, and he never said to me regarding anything I did: "Why did you do it?" nor regarding anything I left undone: "Why did you not do it?"'

The Prophet’s care was not limited to good treatment; he actively cultivated values that build a human being within Anas's heart. He would call him affectionately, 'O my son,' and teach him to go to sleep without holding deceit toward anyone in his heart. He encouraged him to revive the Sunnah and instructed him to spread greetings of peace (Salam) upon his family, clarifying that doing so brings blessing.

After the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away to the Highest Company, Anas lived for over eighty years spreading the knowledge he had received, teaching people the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ until he became a reference point for Muslims whenever they faced difficult matters. What moved his emotions the most were two days that never left his memory: the day the Prophet ﷺ entered Medina, and the day he passed away. He used to say that everything in Medina shone on the day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived, and when he passed away, everything in it became dark.

Allah answered His Prophet's prayer for Anas, blessing him in his life, granting him abundant wealth and a large offspring, to the extent that he saw over a hundred children and grandchildren. Despite all these blessings, his heart remained attached to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, hoping to meet him on the Day of Resurrection, saying, 'I hope to meet the Messenger of Allah ﷺ so I may say to him: O Messenger of Allah, here is your little servant Unays.' As death approached him, he kept repeating, 'There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,' until he met his Lord after a life filled entirely with loyalty to the one who raised and taught him.

steps.title: Key Lessons
steps.content:
1. Proper upbringing begins at home; Anas's mother planted love for the Prophet ﷺ in his heart before he even saw him.

2. Compassion and gentleness in teaching leave a far greater impact than harshness, as demonstrated in the Prophet’s ﷺ treatment of Anas throughout ten years of service.

3. Closeness to people of virtue is a great blessing if invested well in learning and action; Anas capitalized on his companionship with the Prophet ﷺ until he became one of the primary narrators of Hadith.

4. True blessing is not merely in abundant wealth or longevity, but in utilizing these gifts to spread goodness and serve the religion of Allah.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: If you were in Anas's (may Allah be pleased with him) place and lived years alongside a noble role model, what quality would you hope to learn and integrate into your daily life?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Emulate the Prophet ﷺ in one character trait today. Choose to treat a child, a family member, or a colleague with gentleness and patience—even if they make a mistake—and let compassion be your very first response.

title: The Seeker of Truth
subtitle: He departed for Mecca as a leader among his people, returning a believer bearing the light of guidance to his tribe.
heroQuote: «O Allah, grant him a sign to assist him in the good he intends.»
intention: Read today’s journey to reflect on how a fair mind and a sincere heart lead to knowing the truth, remaining steadfast upon it, and calling others to it—no matter how long the path takes.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Al-Tufayl ibn 'Amr Al-Dawsi was the chief of the Daws tribe and one of the prominent Arab nobles renowned for generosity, chivalry, and sound judgment. He was an eloquent poet who could easily distinguish beautiful speech from ugly, making sound decisions on complex matters. He never expected that an ordinary trip to Mecca would change his entire life, turning him into one of the great callers to Islam, and ultimately culminating in his martyrdom for the cause of Allah.

steps.title: From Tribal Chieftainship to Guiding the Way
steps.content:
Al-Tufayl arrived in Mecca at a time when the confrontation between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Quraysh had reached its peak. Barely had he entered Mecca when the leaders of Quraysh surrounded him, warning him sternly against meeting the Prophet ﷺ. They described his call in frightening terms, claiming his speech separated fathers from sons and husbands from their wives, until they convinced him not to listen to a single word from him.

Al-Tufayl was so influenced by what he heard that he placed cotton in his ears when going to the Sacred Mosque (Al-Masjid Al-Haram), fearing that any of the Prophet's ﷺ words might reach him. Yet, as he entered the Mosque, he saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ standing in prayer near the Kaaba. Deeply moved by his appearance and devotion, Allah willed that some of the Quran reached his ears.

Al-Tufayl stood talking to himself, thinking: 'How can I accept judging a man before hearing him out? I am a rational man, capable of distinguishing good from bad. If what he says is good, I will accept it; if it is otherwise, I will leave it.' This decisive thought marked the greatest turning point in his life.

He waited until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned to his home, then followed him inside, recounting what Quraysh had done and how he had stuffed his ears with cotton. He then asked the Prophet ﷺ to present Islam to him. The Prophet ﷺ recited Surah Al-Ikhlas and Surah Al-Falaq. In them, Al-Tufayl found such beauty and divine justice that he had never heard before. He extended his hand, declared the two testimonies of faith (Shahada), and entered Islam out of conviction and certainty.

He stayed in Mecca for a period learning Islam and memorizing what he could of the Quran. He then requested permission from the Prophet ﷺ to return to his tribe to call them to Islam, mentioning that he was an obeyed leader among them, and asked Allah to grant him a sign to assist him in this mission. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed for him, and Allah answered the prayer: a light appeared between his eyes. Fearing his people might consider it a punishment for accepting Islam, he asked Allah to move it, and the light shifted to the tip of his whip, shining for people like a bright lamp.

He began his call with those closest to him. When his father came, Al-Tufayl informed him of his conversion; his father responded, washed and purified himself, learned Islam, and embraced it. Likewise, his wife accepted the message after he explained the truth of monotheism and the absurdity of idol worship.

However, the tribe of Daws did not respond quickly, though Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) was among the first to accept Islam. Al-Tufayl continued calling his people, but their response remained slow, so he returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to report what he experienced. Some Companions assumed the Prophet ﷺ would pray against them, but he raised his hands and said: 'O Allah, guide Daws... O Allah, guide Daws... O Allah, guide Daws.' He then instructed Al-Tufayl to return to his people, treat them gently, and continue inviting them.

Al-Tufayl complied with the Prophet's ﷺ command—never despairing, never growing angry, and never abandoning his mission due to slow results. He spent years among his people inviting them with wisdom and patience until after the Prophet ﷺ migrated to Medina and the battles of Badr, Uhud, and Al-Khandaq took place. Eventually, Al-Tufayl came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ accompanied by eighty households from Daws who had embraced Islam wholeheartedly. The Prophet ﷺ rejoiced and honored them.

After the Conquest of Mecca, Al-Tufayl asked permission from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to destroy his tribe's idol, 'Dhu al-Kaffayn'. The Prophet ﷺ granted him permission. He approached the idol in front of the people while they waited for a calamity to strike him from it. Instead, he set it on fire while reciting his famous verses until it burned to ashes. With its destruction, the last remnants of polytheism vanished from the Daws tribe, and its people entered Islam completely.

After the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Al-Tufayl remained firm on his pledge, fighting alongside Muslims against the apostates during the Caliphate of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him). On his way to the Battle of Yamama, he saw a vision, which he interpreted as glad tidings of his upcoming martyrdom, and that his son 'Amr would follow his path shortly after.

In the Battle of Yamama, Al-Tufayl fought heroically until he achieved martyrdom as he had hoped. His son 'Amr was severely wounded and lost his hand; he lived on until he too attained martyrdom at the Battle of Yarmouk. Thus, Al-Tufayl was a martyr and the father of a martyr.

steps.title: Key Lessons
steps.content:
1. One should never judge the truth based on hearsay or opinions of others; rather, investigate personally and remain objective before passing judgment.

2. A successful caller begins with those closest to them, combining wisdom, gentleness, and patience regardless of how delayed results may seem.

3. Success in inviting others to good is not measured by immediate response; Al-Tufayl persevered for years until his efforts bore fruit in the conversion of his entire tribe.

4. Whoever is sincere in seeking truth and remaining firm upon it, Allah grants them a noble ending—just as He concluded Al-Tufayl's life with martyrdom after a lifetime spent serving Islam.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: Have you ever formed an opinion about a person or idea based solely on what people said, without seeking the truth yourself? How can Al-Tufayl serve as an example for you in fairness and sincere pursuit of truth?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Choose a topic or person you previously held a pre-conceived judgment about. Try to approach it today with fairness, seeking the truth directly from reliable sources before finalizing your opinion.
